neighbours.label: 'that' or 'to' introducing the predicate complement after a plural goal/reason noun plus copula ('the main advantages are that ...', 'its aims are to ...')
fire: The chief benefits of the new law are that it is simple and fair.
The aims of the charity are to feed children and train teachers.
The key findings of the survey were that most people sleep too little.
Our objectives this year are to cut costs and hire more staff.
The usual complaints about the bus are that it is late and crowded.
The duties of a steward were to manage the estate and collect rents.
The main drawbacks of solar panels are that they cost a lot up front.
The goals of the treaty were to end the war and fix the borders.
quiet: The new law is simple and fair, and people like it.
The charity feeds children and trains teachers in rural areas.
The survey found most people sleep too little.
This year we will cut costs and hire more staff.
People often say the bus is late and crowded.
A steward managed the estate and collected the rents.
Solar panels cost a lot up front but save money later.
The treaty ended the war and fixed the borders.

notes: card: ' that'/' to' after 'X are'; probe 0.63-0.79 vs ~0.01 without the copular frame
